The category has the exact shape that failed for security robots: one brand with real US retail presence (Yarbo) and an open question about whether anybody is searching. Four things the SERPs have to settle. FIRST, does the category term return a shopping SERP or a novelty-tech one — the security-robot failure was institutional procurement and encyclopedia entries where consumer intent should have been. SECOND, does the brand swallow the category the way Litter-Robot does, in which case the category term is a redirect to a brand page rather than a hub. THIRD, and the biggest risk here specifically, does the enormous conventional snow-blower market swallow the robot term the way Wirecutter's best pet cameras swallowed 'best pet camera robot' — 'snow blower' and 'best snow blower' are bought as controls for exactly that. FOURTH, and unique to this category: seasonality. Every other category on this site sells year-round. A category whose demand exists for four months is a different commercial proposition from one that does not, and the 12-month trend is bought to measure it rather than to assume it.
